hosting.//: 'main' is the project's original default site (voxmind-504022.web.app). Kept deploying, not decommissioned -- old bookmarks, anything cached, and any doc still pointing at that URL keeps working. 'cu' (voxmind-cu.web.app) is the nicer URL meant to actually be shared going forward. headers.//: Broad rule FIRST, specific rule SECOND -- the reverse of what got deployed first. Two things had to be verified empirically because neither is documented: (1) a header 'source' glob matches the ORIGINAL request path, never the post-rewrite target -- a rule keyed on '/index.html' silently never matched a visitor's actual request for '/', since the SPA rewrite to /index.html happens after header matching. (2) when two header blocks match the same request and set the same key, Firebase applies LAST-match-wins, the opposite of how it documents rewrite-rule precedence ('first rule that matches') -- putting the specific /assets/** rule first and this broad ** rule second silently let the broad rule win for asset requests too, erasing their long-cache header. Order now confirmed correct against the live deployed site for both a page path and a real asset path.

Vite fingerprints these by content hash, so a given URL's bytes can never change -- caching them for a year is safe, and it's the rule that must win for anything under /assets/, overriding the broad rule above by coming after it.

Clickjacking matters more than usual here. This app asks for camera and microphone permission, and the classic attack is to frame the real site invisibly over a decoy so the victim clicks 'Allow' believing it belongs to another page.
Stops a browser from second-guessing a Content-Type and executing something served as data.
Send the full URL only to ourselves. Other origins get the bare origin, so a path that identifies a user or device never leaks in a Referer header.

The most valuable header for this project: camera and microphone are usable by this origin and denied to every embedded frame. Anything the page embeds is cut off from the sensors regardless of what it asks for.
